exposure: labor induction methods (cervical balloon dilation, oxytocin, spontaneous labor)
outcome: neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission rates
cohort: Primiparous women with singleton, full-term pregnancies, categorized by the presence or absence of Group B Streptococcus (GBS) colonization at 35-37 weeks' gestation.
finding: Among GBS-colonized women, cervical balloon dilation was associated with increased maternal infection and intrapartum fever, and both cervical balloon dilation and oxytocin induction methods resulted in higher cesarean section rates compared to spontaneous labor, with no impact on neonatal adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: Both cervical balloon dilation and oxytocin induction methods were associated with higher cesarean section rates compared to spontaneous labor among GBS-colonized women.
